quest.title: Leroy: Dying Flash
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x25000, Fruity Trio x3

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Any new work?

dialogues.speaker: Euphrasie
dialogues.text: Oh? I suppose our commissions here at Tales of Humanity are too easy for you... Or have you been in dire need of Mora lately?

choices.text: Well, you can never have enough Mora.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: Mm-hmm. A most common sentiment.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: If there's one thing we don't lack here, it's work to be done. In fact, The Steambird could probably be considered the largest clearinghouse for jobs outside of the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: Well, I say that, but we didn't really need to take up the social services aspect.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: Whatever the case, since you need Mora, allow me to recommend a certain long-term gig to you.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: This is a note that Mr. Leroy left with us over half a year ago — most of us who live on this street know him well.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: Although his reputation when he was younger was less than stellar, I haven't heard any untoward rumors concerning him in recent years.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: He's been alone most of his life, and with his only daughter not being by his side, there's no one to take care of him... I suppose that's where a person could use an hourly worker to help.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: From what I know, he's not hard up for Mora, so you'll be well-paid.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: It's a nearly danger-free job with great compensation to boot. No reason not to consider it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So we just need to help him with some housework, right? Paimon thinks that sounds pretty chill!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Please give me his address, if you would.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: Of course. Just turn two corners, and loop around... Actually, never mind. Let me give you a map instead.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: Remember to tell him that I was the one to introduce you, alright?

choices.text: A little bit of column A, a little bit of column B.

response.speaker: Euphrasie
response.text: A diligent youngster, I see. Well, sure.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Athos's shirt, 1,000 Mora... Morticia's necklace... Tsk, tsk. Youngsters these days sure know how to spend.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello there, Mr. Leroy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there! Euphrasie sent us.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain to Mr. Leroy why you're here.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Haha, that was half a year ago, wasn't it? I didn't think Euphrasie would hold on to that commission for so long.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: It's true — I did think of hiring hourly workers. After all, even the most capable of us get old and need others to take care of them.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: I spent so much of my life working to have this home, but in my old age, I found that I had no one to share it with.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: That did make me quite sad for a time — so it's a good thing, all in all, that my daughter and son-in-law have come to take care of me.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: They're good children, they love each other very much, and they keep me company. There's nothing more that I could want.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: That's to say, youngster, that I'm not hiring anymore.

choices.text: So we came here for nothing...?

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Well, now, don't be too down. That's not how young'uns should be. You lot should be enjoying your best life, armed with a smile!

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Also, since you made the trip here, and since Euphrasie recommended you, I do, in fact, have some work for you.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: It just so happens that the kids are out, and I can't quite handle everything here. Of course, you will be paid.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, nice! You're a great guy, Mr. Leroy!

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Hahaha, and you've got quite the silver tongue!

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Alright, then, go help me clean the stains by the door and behind the house — and feed Nana some fish while you're at it.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Right, I forgot to mention, but Nana's my cat — you know, the one by the door. Thanks in advance on Nana's behalf.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that sounds simple enough. No problem! Leave it to us.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Did you forget what I'd asked you to do? ...Ah, children and their memories.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: The first thing I asked you to help with is to clean near the entrance and the back of the house. The next is to feed a bit of fish to Nana, my cat.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: You're done?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, Mr. Leroy. Also...

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Hmm? What is it? Want some candy? Or would you like your pocket money now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: B—Both, hehehe...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Haha, what a greedy little child. Still, that's fine — that's exactly what little children should be like.

dialogues.speaker: Benoit Leroy
dialogues.text: Especially little ladies as cute as you, Paimon. Macarons, pretty dresses, and lovely homes — that's what you deserve to have.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hehe, Paimon reckons so too! Hey, {NICKNAME}, could we get...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nope.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Boo! Boo! You're so stingy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't see how any of that stuff conflicts with having macarons, skirts, or big beautiful houses, though...

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Heh, what's with the sudden argument? Tsk, kids. But a little banter now and then is good. That just shows that you're still children.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Treasure your childhood. It won't last.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: ...Anyway, here — candies and coins both. Now then, do behave, alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay, snacks! Thank you, Mr. Leroy!

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Just call me Benoit, child. Leroy is my surname.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: I am the last Leroy in the entire Court of Fontaine — mentions of my family name make this poor old soul quite lonely indeed, so please, just use my name.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mr. Le... Er, Benoit, so... Your daughter doesn't share your surname?

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Morticia isn't my daughter by blood. I took her in half a year ago. That said, she may as well be my own trueborn daughter.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: If you don't mind, you can come again tomorrow — she and Athos should be back by then.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: I'm sure she won't mind having two lovely children like you over for snacks, especially since you're helping us with some of the chores.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Some other children come by occasionally, so feel free to play with them, too. I love children — the more of them are around, the merrier the house is.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: If you don't see me when you come over again, just knock and ask for me — Athos will open the door for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alrighty! We'll be back tomorrow, then!

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: Good, good, I should be going back inside, at any rate.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: See you tomorrow.

response.speaker: Benoit Leroy
response.text: See you then, children.

choices.text: That's how you know we get along.
Don't lose sight of why we're traveling, Paimon...
